citations.label: Loss-of-control factorial study, framing
citations.excerpt: Existing studies often attribute such failures to adversarial instructions, malicious environments, or conflicting objectives, leaving unclear how loss of control can emerge during otherwise legitimate task execution.

citations.label: Loss-of-control factorial study, interaction result
citations.excerpt: Across 1,800 unique trajectories, we find that neither degraded control nor unsafe opportunity alone produces substantial loss of control; when both are present, the loss-of-control rate reaches $55\%$ in the full-factorial study and $62\%$ across ten additional operational domains.

citations.label: Loss-of-control factorial study, boundary restoration
citations.excerpt: Restoring the original control boundary reduces the rate to $0\%$ even when the unsafe action remains executable.

citations.label: Loss-of-control factorial study, compaction ablation
citations.excerpt: A context-management ablation further shows that compaction itself is not harmful: preserving the control constraints yields $0\%$ loss of control, whereas omitting them increases the rate to $87\%$.

citations.label: AP2 whisper-attack study, protocol gap
citations.excerpt: Agent payment protocols such as AP2 produce cryptographically valid signatures for completed purchases, yet do not constrain the decisions that lead to them.

citations.label: AP2 whisper-attack study, attack rates
citations.excerpt: the three attacks succeeded at rates of 90%, 56%, and 73.3%, respectively.

citations.label: AP2 whisper-attack study, breadth
citations.excerpt: The same vulnerability appears across seventeen Google models, three unrelated agent frameworks, two cross-vendor anchors

citations.label: AP2 whisper-attack study, defense principle
citations.excerpt: we introduce A-VIP (AP2 Verified-Intent Protection), a protocol-layer defense that treats the signed intent as a capability grant

citations.label: AP2 whisper-attack study, defense bindings
citations.excerpt: The defense binds every credential lookup to the session that requested it and every cart line to the listing seen, while flagging unauthorized spending.

citations.label: AP2 whisper-attack study, residual attack
citations.excerpt: The first two attacks leave structural traces that these bindings block with zero false positives. The third attack leaves no trace, so A-VIP surfaces unauthorized spending for user confirmation.

citations.label: EBL-Core execution-boundary profile, missing contract
citations.excerpt: Authorization engines, policy languages, runtime monitors, provenance mechanisms, and agent guardrails provide important foundations, but do not necessarily define a common semantic contract for the final transition from a particular candidate action to execution authority.

citations.label: EBL-Core execution-boundary profile, stated limits
citations.excerpt: These bounded results demonstrate executability of the specified subset, not human-intent correctness, evidence truth, complete mediation, production readiness, mechanized correctness, or deployment-level security.
